parts:
There are a lot of different options for how you encode the data, but yes for crosstype "risib" you need to code genotypes according to the founders' alleles, and A/B is one choice that could work.

The BXD mouse RIL are one example dataset to look at:

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] RIL fullsib population
parts:
The heatmap plotting function is not so critical as the actual
calculations, which aren't yet available in R/qtl2.
There's nothing to calculate and then transfer back to R/qtl1, at present.

You can try doing genome scans to look for interactions with particular
QTL, by using scan1() with the genotype probabilities for a specific
location as interactive covariates with the intcovar argument. You
could, in principle, repeat that for every location, and
roll-your-own-scan2().

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] RIL fullsib population
parts:
You shouldn’t need to rerun scan1(). You just need a physical map that corresponds to the genetic map you used in calc_genoprob(). If you had used insert_pseudomarkers(), then you would need to use interp_map() to get interpolated positions for the pseudomarkers. 

lod_int() and bayes_int() take the scan1 output and a map; the map could be genetic or physical positions.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] RIL fullsib population
parts:
scan1 requires that the first argument be a "calc_genoprob" object, as output by calc_genoprob. So that'll be a list of 3-d arrays, one per chromosome, with the 3d arrays being like individuals x genotypes x positions.

The intcovar argument needs to be a numeric matrix, individuals x covariates. And the row names need to be the individual names.

The lack of the individual names is what the error message is about, but I think the problem in your code is larger than that.

I presume that "pr" is an object with genotype probabilities, and that B02 is one of the chromosomes. And then you're trying to pull out the 2nd and 363rd positions? You'd need to do pr$B02[,,2] and pr$B02[,,363]. Those should each then be matrices with individuals as rows.

But you can't use scan1 on a single position. And you wouldn't want to include all of the genotype columns as covariates; you need to drop one of them since the probabilities sum to 1.

So maybe try:

intco <- pr$B02[ , -1, 363, drop=FALSE]
output <- scan1(pr[,"B02"], pheno=RILs$pheno, kinship=kinship_loco$B02,
                intcovar=intco)

karl

On Friday, 5 June 2020 18:04:17 UTC-3, Karl Broman wrote:
scan1 requires that the first argument be a "calc_genoprob" object, as output by calc_genoprob. So that'll be a list of 3-d arrays, one per chromosome, with the 3d arrays being like individuals x genotypes x positions.

The intcovar argument needs to be a numeric matrix, individuals x covariates. And the row names need to be the individual names.

The lack of the individual names is what the error message is about, but I think the problem in your code is larger than that.

I presume that "pr" is an object with genotype probabilities, and that B02 is one of the chromosomes. And then you're trying to pull out the 2nd and 363rd positions? You'd need to do pr$B02[,,2] and pr$B02[,,363]. Those should each then be matrices with individuals as rows.

But you can't use scan1 on a single position. And you wouldn't want to include all of the genotype columns as covariates; you need to drop one of them since the probabilities sum to 1.

So maybe try:

intco <- pr$B02[ , -1, 363, drop=FALSE]
output <- scan1(pr[,"B02"], pheno=RILs$pheno, kinship=kinship_loco$B02,
                intcovar=intco)

karl
